tone_statements.quote: XZ Lalo shares the same syllable template as YL: (C)V(N)T, in which the optional initial is one of 30 consonants, an obligatory vowel (one of 13 vowels or 1 syllabic fricative), an optional nasal final /-,/, and tone (one of 4). All tones are in modal phonation. … Unlike any other Lalo variety, XZ has merged *3, *H, *L to the mid level tone [33]. The resulting system contrasts four tones: High, Mid, Low, and Low-rising, as seen in Table 3-46 below. … The Tone *1 split and merger of *3, *H and *L leaves XZ with three equally spaced level tones and one rising tone.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.8 'XZ' (pp. 96-98) is a segment-and-tone sketch: syllable template (C)V(N)T, 30 initials, 13 vowels + syllabic fricative, nasal final, 4 tones (High 55 [453], Low-rising 24, Low 21, Mid 33), all modal phonation; sec. 5.3.4 gives acoustic tone plots. No statement on word stress/accent anywhere in the thesis; the only 'stressed' is incidental, in the CW-QY (Qingyun, West Mountain) sketch: 'Following a stressed syllable, the syllabic nasal loses its syllabicity'. p. 3: Ngwi languages such as Lalo are 'omnisyllabic' (almost every syllable assigned a lexical tone).

All tones are in modal phonation. … Unlike any other Lalo variety, XZ has merged *3, *H, *L to the mid level tone [33]. tone.says: Four tones on every (C)V(N) syllable, all modal voice: high 55 (often [453] in isolation), mid 33, low 21 and low-rising 24; three level tones and one rising; F0 plots of one speaker.
